newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour says windfall levy will be one-off.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour says windfall levy will be one-off.

text.p: Gordon Brown, finance spokesman for Britain's opposition Labour party, said his planned windfall tax on the profits of privatised utilities would be a one-off levy to reduce youth unemployment.
"This is a one-off levy, I've made that absolutely clear," he told BBC radio.
"It will work and we are utterly satisfied that the three billion pound employment programme that we are proposing and outlining today will be comfortably financed within the windfall levy."

"It is one-off, it will be levied fairly. There will be consultation with the regulators and it is restricted only to these privatised utilities that were sold off at an under-valuation and have had lax regulatory regimes." Asked about comments by Labour's parliamentary business manager Donald Dewar about possible tax adjustments under Labour, Brown replied:
"What Donald Dewar was talking about was, for example, our proposal to cut VAT on fuel (and) my long-term aim to get a 10 pence starting rate of income tax."
